title: Angles and trigonometric foundations
purpose: Connect angle measure, triangle ratios, and circle coordinates so later trigonometric formulas have meaning.

lessons.title: Radians, rotations, and arc length
lessons.objective: Convert degree and radian measures, identify coterminal angles, and calculate an arc length with consistent units.
lessons.coverage: Directed rotations and standard position; exact degree, radian and turn conversion; decimal and degree-minute-second measures; coterminal families, requested representative intervals, quadrants and axes, strict acute reference angles, arc and sector relationships, compatible units, radius scaling, multiple turns, uniform angular/tangential motion and piecewise reversals.
lessons.activity: Set a radius and an angle, predict the arc length, and compare the same angle at two radii using a numeric form and a circle diagram.
families: Convert exact pi-fraction angles and locate their quadrant
Compute arc length or sector area and identify a degree/radian mismatch
lessons.generatorRules: Use positive radii and positive elapsed durations where required; include zero motion, signed rotations, ordinary radian values, negative angles, multiple turns and interval boundaries. Preserve exact pi and complete-turn information. Distinguish signed displacement from nonnegative travel, arc from chord, and unique sector area from repeated coverage. Apply s=r*theta and v=r*omega only with matching radian and time units. State no-slip and uniform-motion premises when used.
lessons.commonError: Substituting degrees into a radian formula or assuming a negative angle has negative magnitude of physical arc length when a distance is asked.
lessons.feedback: Compare the requested quantity with a full circumference and distinguish directed displacement from distance.
lessons.checkpoint: Conversion, coterminal angle, reference angle, and arc-length calculation.

lessons.title: Right-triangle ratios
lessons.objective: Choose a trigonometric ratio to solve a right triangle and interpret the solution with the correct reference angle and units.
lessons.coverage: Opposite/adjacent relative to an angle, hypotenuse, sine/cosine/tangent ratios, complementary angles, special triangles, and angle-of-elevation models.
lessons.activity: Relabel a fixed triangle from either acute angle and predict how the opposite and adjacent sides swap while the hypotenuse stays fixed.
families: Find a missing side or angle of a right triangle
Translate a diagram or accessible text description into the appropriate ratio
lessons.generatorRules: Generate valid positive triangles; include exact special-angle cases and approximate measured cases. Avoid premature rounding of a side used in a later calculation.
lessons.commonError: Naming sides independently of the chosen angle or selecting a reciprocal ratio.
lessons.feedback: Mark the reference angle and locate the hypotenuse before writing any ratio.
lessons.checkpoint: Ratio selection, exact special-triangle value, side computation, and application with units.

lessons.title: The unit circle and exact values
lessons.objective: Determine exact sine and cosine values using coordinates, symmetry, reference angles, and quadrant signs.
lessons.coverage: The point (cos(theta),sin(theta)), 30/45/60-degree reference triangles, quadrantal angles, periodicity, negative angles, and sin^2+cos^2=1.
lessons.activity: Predict the coordinate signs and exact pair before moving to a selected angle; all tasks are available through typed angles and a coordinate table.
families: Evaluate exact sine/cosine pairs for special and coterminal angles
Recover possible coordinates or angle locations from one coordinate and a quadrant
lessons.generatorRules: Represent exact values with rational numbers and square roots, not floating-point answer matching. Include axis points and negative angles.
lessons.commonError: Swapping sine and cosine coordinates or applying the reference-angle magnitude without its quadrant sign.
lessons.feedback: Locate x and y signs first, then choose the reference-triangle magnitudes.
lessons.checkpoint: An exact pair, a negative angle, a quadrantal angle, and a coordinate/quadrant reconstruction.

lessons.title: All six trigonometric functions
lessons.objective: Calculate the six trigonometric ratios where defined and explain each undefined value using a zero denominator.
lessons.coverage: Tangent/cotangent as coordinate ratios, secant/cosecant as reciprocals, reciprocal versus inverse-function notation, parity, and period differences.
lessons.activity: Use a coordinate pair to construct all six values, highlighting the denominators and predicting where a function becomes undefined.
families: Derive the remaining ratios from one ratio and a quadrant
Classify exact values, undefined cases, and parity/period statements
lessons.generatorRules: Keep undefined answers distinct from infinity and from a very large finite approximation. If only one ratio is provided, add enough sign/quadrant information for a unique requested result.
lessons.commonError: Reporting tan(pi/2) as a large finite calculator value or confusing reciprocal notation with arcsine/arccosine.
lessons.feedback: Replace the function with its coordinate ratio and inspect the denominator exactly.
lessons.checkpoint: Ratio reconstruction, undefined value, reciprocal-versus-inverse distinction, and parity/period reasoning.

anchor.prompt: Find sine, cosine, and tangent at 5*pi/6 radians.
anchor.answer: sin=1/2, cos=-sqrt(3)/2, tan=-sqrt(3)/3. The angle is in quadrant II, so sine is positive and cosine and tangent are negative.

moduleExit: Demonstrate exact unit-circle values without relying on a calculator and recognize undefined ratios through their denominators.
